lastCompletedStory.title: WARNING: Site 4 is the only one of the five CAM-510 sites with no stale-sibling pruning

openQuestions: CAM-513 (flaky-test-isolation, filed on main from US-R1-003) remains open and unrelated to this story's diff.
nextStoryContext: US-R2-005 closed the reviewer's WARNING that site 4 (src/commands/setup.ts, the cam-cli-config-log parent directory holding the v|V viewer's <pid>.log/.chunk/.lock siblings) was the only one of CAM-510's five leak sites shipped with no stale-sibling pruning: cleanup depended entirely on the menu script's own EXIT trap (buildConfigLogCleanupCommand), so an abnormal menu-pane termination (tmux kill-pane, SIGKILL, crash) left <pid>.log/.chunk/.lock under the fixed parent forever. Added: (1) CONFIG_LOG_PARENT_DIR_NAME, an exported string constant ('cam-cli-config-log') shared between configLogDirExpr()'s bash-expression form (resolved later by the spawned pane's own shell) and the new TS-side resolution, so the two can never drift apart; (2) pruneStaleConfigLogSiblings(parent), a private helper that reads the fixed parent's direct children and rmSync's (force:true) any entry whose mtime is older than STALE_CONFIG_LOG_AGE_MS (one hour, matching STALE_PID_DIR_AGE_MS/STALE_VERSION_DIR_AGE_MS at the other four CAM-510 sites); (3) pruneStaleConfigLogDir(), the exported production entry point (mkdirSync the parent + prune), called from spawnSetupTmux before every `cam setup` run, before the new pane's own $$-namespaced files are ever created. Unlike the other four sites (which nest by pid into a SUBdirectory and skip ownPidDirName because their prune call runs AFTER their own subdirectory already exists), site 4's directory is flat (files sit directly in the parent) and the prune call runs BEFORE this invocation's own files exist, so every entry is pruned independently by age with no 'own' exemption needed -- documented as an accepted tradeoff (same one already accepted at the other four sites): a viewer session open longer than the one-hour threshold could have its .lock sibling (whose mtime is set once at loop start and never touched again while the writer runs) pruned by a LATER cam setup invocation while its .log is still being actively appended. Added 4 new tests to test/setup-config-log.test.ts (new describe block 'pruneStaleConfigLogDir'): parent-dir creation under redirected TMPDIR, no-throw on a not-yet-existing parent, a GOTCHA-8-style stale-trio-pruned/recent-sibling-survives test (mirrors test/release/ship-pr-tempfile.test.ts's convention, using utimesSync to backdate mtimes), and a cross-check that the TS-side resolved parent and the real bash-side buildConfigLogPathAssignment's resolved log path (spawned under the same redirected TMPDIR) agree on the same fixed parent. Full bun test 6109 pass / 0 fail (+4 from the new tests), typecheck 0 errors, full bun run check:all spine green after one justified gate resolution: file-size-budget.json raised for src/commands/setup.ts (1141->1223, the new pruneStaleConfigLogDir/pruneStaleConfigLogSiblings functions plus their doc comments and the shared CONFIG_LOG_PARENT_DIR_NAME constant), dated note prepended to _ref naming this story/CAM-510 and staged in the same commit. No knip/jscpd/coverage changes needed; no vendor/templates changes, no embed-vendor needed. Step 5.5 (WebFetch against the current Node.js os.tmpdir() docs) confirmed os.tmpdir() checks TMPDIR (then TMP, then TEMP) on POSIX, falling back to /tmp if none are set -- matches bash's ${TMPDIR:-/tmp} closely enough for the realistic case (TMPDIR set, the only case either side actually needs to agree on), no correction needed. scripts/cam/prd.json was left untouched/uncommitted by this story, per the AGENT.md rule that the implementer never edits prd.json.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed os.tmpdir() on POSIX checks TMPDIR, then TMP, then TEMP, falling back to /tmp if none are set -- consistent with bash's ${TMPDIR:-/tmp} resolution used by configLogDirExpr() for the realistic TMPDIR-set case that both the TS-side prune and the bash-side path assignment need to agree on.
